messages:
elena: quick heads-up — during a quant4-v2 bring-up I hit a reproducible divergence after ~8k tokens when using warmed heads + prefill stitching. logs: `s3://ci-logs/ropex/1737778888/warmhead-flip.log`

samir: can you paste the minimal repro? idea: warmhead twin priming might be colliding with prefix eviction.

elena: repro script below, small loop that alternates two long priming sequences then continues generation. i ran it on a single shard.
```bash
# repro gist
python tools/repro_longpriming.py --model quant4-v2 --priming-file priming_a.txt --alt-file priming_b.txt --steps 10000
```

jun: whats the divergence symptom? token shift, garbled text, or perf drop?

elena: token shift + occasional hallucinated token duplication around the warmhead boundary. not latency-related. model starts repeating a 3-token pattern anchored to the earlier prefix.

mika: interesting — could be RoPE wrap/scale mismatch when we stitch KV segments from different priming phases. any index traces?

elena: i dumped kvcache keys/positions and saw twin entries that map to same rotary index but different position offsets. sample: `pos 8190 -> rot_idx 4095` and `pos 8191 -> rot_idx 0` then after wrap we observed `pos 1 -> rot_idx 1` but the values from 8191 ended up at pos 1 on next segment.

samir: that sounds like an off-by-one in the post-shard wrap arithmetic. have you tried forcing modulo behavior in the index calc to validate?

elena: yes i patched the local runtime to use `(pos % window)` explicit and the repro went away in 3 runs. but that's just a local patch — need to confirm with quantized kernels.

jun: re: quantized kernels: int4 packing reorders bytes; if our kvcache copy path slices by bytes vs tokens we could accidentally shift. can you run with `KERNEL_DEBUG=1`?

elena: run attached with KERNEL_DEBUG. output shows memcpy offsets aligned to bytes, not tokens. snippet: `memcpy(dst + 32, src + 30, 64) // expected 30 tokens -> but kernels operate in 16-byte lanes`

mika: aha. hypothesis: packed int4 stride (nibbles per token) + prefill window boundary cause a half-lane shift when priming alternates. That would explain duplication/ghost tokens.

samir: next steps: 1) reproduce without warmhead twin (single long priming) 2) reproduce with explicit modulo fix 3) run quantized and fp16 kernels to compare. i'll take #1 and #3.

elena: thanks — i'm running the explicit modulo fix on a dedicated instance to test at scale (5k runs). i'll post metrics.

perf-bot: ci-run 1737778896: warmhead-modulo-fix smoke: PASS (3/3) — latency ok, small perf regression +1.8%

jun: good start. if modulo fix passes, we should add a kernel-level assert to detect half-lane shifts during memcpy in debug builds. also add a unit test that alternates two priming buffers across the wrap boundary.

mika: i'll sketch a patch for the int4 memcpy slice to ensure token-aligned copies. putting a draft on the PR: `github.com/redwood-inference/rt/PR-xxxx`

elena: posting the full dump and a short write-up in the ticket: https://redwood.local/issue/ML-1729 — summary: warmhead twin priming + quant packing can cause KV misalign by half-lane on wrap; local modulo guard mitigates.

samir: once we have kernel patch, run large longctx benchmark (50k tokens) and compare sample fidelity vs baseline. watch for any subtle regression in coherence metrics (per-token surprisal drift).

elena: ack. i'll coordinate with perf to schedule a run tomorrow morning. thanks all :thumbsup:
